prompt: Which conditions define a non-strict partial order $R$ on a set $A$?

answers.explanation: Antisymmetry makes mutual comparison imply equality; unlike a total order, incomparable elements are allowed.
This defines a strict partial order.
This allows only diagonal pairs but need not include all of them.
A preorder may relate two distinct elements in both directions.
Reflexivity is missing; an empty relation on a nonempty set satisfies both.
Transitivity is missing; a two-step chain may lack its shortcut.
This additionally requires totality, excluding partial orders with incomparable elements.
Adding symmetry restricts the relation to equality.
Asymmetry forbids self-loops and thus gives the strict, not non-strict, notion.

sources.title: ANU Logic Notes — Relations: properties and orderings
